doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

chapter: Buddy Rich, Sinatra and the Stones
title: Playing the Sinatra book
summary: Davis recalls being the young man in Sinatra's band and the quality of the Riddle, May, Mandel, Jenkins and Costa charts.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: And what about, let’s see Buddy Rich, Rolling Stones, Frank Sinatra?
Couldn’t play with anybody good, ey?

Yeah, I’m grateful for all the opportunities I’ve had. It’s been a terrific run. And if somebody would have told me 42 years ago when I got out of Eastman, “Here’s what you’re going to do would you take it right now?” I would take it in a heartbeat. And Sinatra was awesome. I mean when I started I was kind of the young guy on the band and the older guys who had been there for a long time, most of which are passed on now, they were really super great to me. They took me under their wing and the stories were incredible. And also that book of music to me is — there’ll never be a collection of arrangements that good again. Because not to say there aren’t great arrangers because there certainly are, but every one of those, you know when Sinatra picked up the phone so to speak, you know those arrangers brought their A game to the highest degree. So whether you’re playing a Billy May chart or a Nelson Riddle chart, which Nelson was probably the most associated with Frank, or Johnny Mandel, or Gordon Jenkins or Don Costa. These — they were all — every chart is a 10. And so for me as a young person getting to play that book, I loved every minute of it. It was awesome and you’re just hearing these absolute gems. You can’t play it wrong. You know you might crack a note but the figures are so beautifully constructed and the voicings and everything, it’s just everything was exactly the way you’d want to do it. And all of these — they were such

— well the arrangements still exist — they’re just such absolute gems. And so it’s unlikely that there would be a big band that would have that many different arrangers with different styles but all be that great. So it was a very special book of music to get to play on a nightly basis.
